purpose: Progressive-disclosure manifest for one governed Freedom 250 research package.
title: CLARITY Act — September 2026 Senate Draft
question: What did the September 14, 2026 Senate draft of the CLARITY Act change, and what happened when it reached the floor?
bluf: The Senate failed to end debate on the CLARITY Act on September 15, 49–50, so the September 14 sponsors' draft was never formally offered. That draft had made a crypto ethics rule for officials permanent (divest, or move to a blind trust, crypto-company stakes of $15,000 or more, enforceable by state attorneys general), added a circuit breaker requiring Treasury to ban comparable yield if stablecoin rewards drain small banks, and generally barred registered crypto exchanges from trading for themselves. Two days after the vote the CFTC sent its own crypto-market rule to White House review; the agencies already hold most of the tools, and the main gap is plain spot trading of crypto that isn't a security.
evidence_cutoff_note: Draft text as released September 14; the September 15 cloture result is recorded in the CFTC passive-software study.
use_note: Catalog entry added 2026-10-03 (crypto hub clean-up) so this work can be found on its own; its files stay where they are and remain members of the parent study.

retrieval_instructions: Open full_text_url for the package before treating a summary as the underlying research.
For a public reading, prefer reading_url. For public_machine_data, open data_url and preserve its schema_version, data_as_of, scope_boundary and evidence vocabulary.
A failure to retrieve public_full_text is an access or crawler problem, not a private-by-design signal.
For access_state private_by_design, use metadata only and do not infer contents.
Preserve the package evidence cutoff, evidence_cutoff_note and any material-specific as_of date. Verify time-sensitive claims with fresh primary sources.
Keep fact, project inference, strongest rival, unresolved object and falsifier separate.
